Commentary.Commentary: New Zealand will feel they are on top but England did not let the visitors run away with the game. The wicket is still a good one to bat on so they would want to cash in on it. The Kiwis will hope to take 2 or even more before the deficit is erased. A good little passage of play awaits before Tea. Can England enter the break unscathed?

The Kiwis will be a little disappointed with the lead! Their top order really batted well. Young, Conway and Taylor all scored half tons. All three of them were dismissed in the 80s and none could make it into a big one. However, because of them, 400-plus looked possible but the middle and the lower-order failed to make most of the starts they got and they end a little below that mark.

End of a really good bowling performance in this session! They had 5 wickets to take and they have taken it quickly. Stone, Broad, Anderson and Wood took one at least and in the end, they kept the lead under 100.
An appeal for an LBW has been turned down. England review.

OUT! Three reds and that is the end of the Kiwi innings! Good review from England. There were two sounds but it did not hit the bat. On middle, Patel looks to heave it across the line but misses. It hits the pad. An appeal but turned down. England review and it shows the on-field call needs to be overturned. NEW ZEALAND HAVE BEEN BOWLED OUT FOR 388!
FOUR! Great Shot! Tossed up, on off. Boult shimmys down the pitch and slashes it over bowlers head, down the ground for four.
On middle. Clips it towards square leg for single.
Round arm from Root, spills it down the leg side. Patel misses his flick.
Floated on middle. Flicked towards mid-wicket.
On middle. Defended back on the crease.
Tossed up, outside off. Watchfully left alone.
Outside off. Left alone.
FOUR! Lead is now of 80! Back of a length ball, on middle. Boult looks to pull but gets inner half of bat past mid-on for four.
Yorker and on middle. Digs out to mid on.
FOUR! Cheeky! Full and on middle. Boult looks to heave it on leg side but gets a thick inside edge towards the fine leg fence for four.
On middle, Kept out.
Shot but well Fielded! Full and on middle. Boult makes room and pushes it wide of mid-on who dives to his left and saves a boundary.
Full and on middle. Patel flicks it towards mid-wicket for two more runs.
FOUR! Consecutive Boundaries! Angles this one on middle. Patel sways down and upper cuts it towards the over the first slip fielder for a boundary.
FOUR! Timing! Angles this one onto the pads. Patel whips it towards the mid-wicket region for four.
Short and on middle. Patel pulls it along the ground towards mid-wicket for couple of runs.
Full and on off. Patel guides it out to the point fielder who dives to his left and denies a single.
Back of a length ball, on middle. Patel pulls it off back foot towards square leg for single.
Length and outside off. Left alone.
On middle. Kept out.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Number 9 goes down and it is Blundell who is the last recognized batter. That is a good catch by Root. This is full and outside off, Blundell goes for an expansive drive. This flies off the outside edge and Root takes a good catch to his left.
Commentary.Howout: c Joe Root b Stuart Broad

Commentary.Commentary: Yorker and on middle. Blundell digs it out in time towards mid-wicket.
A length ball, angling on middle. Blundell watchfully blocks it.
Fuller and on off. Blundell defends this under his eyes.
Stuart Broad is back!
DRINKS! A good hour for England! They have managed to take wickets on regular intervals but they need to keep doing so. The lead has already crossed 50, ca they take the remaining two quickly?
A short of  length ball, on middle. Patel sways away from it.
FOUR! Freebie! Low full toss, outside off. Patel makes room and guides it through the vacant gully region for four.
Fuller and on middle. Patel defends it to covers.
Another length ball, outside off. Shoulders arms to it.
Short ball, Angling on middle. Patel sways away from it.
Tad fuller and on middle. This is flicked towards mid-wicket for a quick single.
Swing and a miss! Length ball, outside off. Patel looks to pull it but misses it.
Another one on the middle. Patel solidly defends this back on the crease.
On middle. Blocked out.
Tad fuller and on middle. Patel shows the full face of bat and defends it on the off side.
On middle. Kept out.
Full and on middle. Patel defends it to mid on.
Length ball, angling on the pads. Patel looks to flick but misses, the ball rolls over, wide of short leg for a Leg Bye.
Length ball, angling on middle. Blocked out.
Fuller and angling on off. Patel drives it to the point fielder.
Good Bowling! A short of a length ball, angling in on middle. Patel ducks and sways away from it.
On middle, Kept out.
Back of a length ball, on middle. Patel ducks under this one to let it fly towards the keeper.
On middle. This is flicked towards fine leg for a single.
Full and on off. Patel blocks it out.
On middle, this is worked through mid-wicket for one.
Length ball, and on off. Blundell defends this on the crease.
On middle. Kept out.
Shout for LBW but might be missing the leg stump! Full and drifting on leg stump. Blundell looks to flick but misses. Hits the pads. Anderson shouts for LBW but was clearly missing the leg stump.
Back of a length ball, outside off. Patel sways away from it.
Round the wicket. A length ball, outside off. Patel shoulders arms to it.
Ajaz Patel walks out to bat!

OUT! THAT LOOKED OUT FROM THE TIME IT HIT THE PAD! Too quick for Henry. Wood spears this one full and around middle and leg. Henry looks to flick but is a touch late in getting the bat down. He misses and it hits the back pad. An appeal and the finger is raised. England really bowling with a lot of fire here.
Length and on middle. Clipped towards mid-wicket.
On middle. Kept out.
Outside off. Pushed towards cover.
On middle. Kept out.
A length ball, on middle. This is flicked to the mid-wicket region.
Tad fuller, outside off. Prods forward and defends this to covers.
Full and on middle. It is clipped towards the mid-wicket fielder.
On middle. blocked out.
Full and drifting down the leg side. Blundell misses his flick to the keeper.
FOUR! Length ball, outside off. Henry slashes it hard but gets a thick edge over the leaping 2nd slip fielder for a boundary.
Full and on off. Henry middles this one for a push towards mid-off who dives to his right and saves a boundary.
FOUR! A length ball, outside off. Henry drives this under his eyes through the cover-point fielder for four.
Fuller and on middle. This is on-driven to the mid-on fielder.
On middle. Blocked out.
Fuller and on off. This is driven but straight to the cover fielder.
On off, kept out.
On off, it is pushed to cover.
Solid again! Another one on middle, it is played back to the bowler.
On middle again, this is defended nicely.
Back of a length and on off, this is pushed to covers.
On off, kept out.
FOUR! Back of a length ball, on off. Henry half-pulls it through the mid-wicket fielder for four.
Short and on middle. It is pulled towards fine leg for a single.
FOUR! Full and outside off. Blundell leans into the drive and plays it through covers for four.
This is Good Bowling by England! A cross-seamer on middle. Blundell looks to flick but gets tangled and gets hit on pads of a inside edge.
Another length ball, on middle. This is worked towards mid-wicket.
On middle. Kept out.
A huge appeal but turned down. Root reviews. Seems high.

NOT OUT! There is a spike on Ultra Edge so England lose their review! Never looked out to be honest. Not sure why the review was taken. Maybe in excitement. This is shortish and angling into the pads. Henry looks to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads. An appeal but turned down. Anderson does not fancy it a lot but Root reviews. Replays show that there is an inside edge.
Another dot as this is pushed to cover.
On middle. Defended back to bowler.
Matt Henry is the bee man in.

OUT! Bowled! Two in two overs for England! Anderson goes around the wicket, bowls a length ball, angling in around off. Hint of inswing, Wagner tries to push at it but was too late to his shot, and the ball knocks off the stumps. This is a good passage of play for England.
On middle. Defended back to bowler.
Length ball, on middle. Flicked on to leg side for a single.

Good Bowling! Back of a length ball, on middle. Wagner was in two minds whether to duck or to defend. Ends up defending, the ball hits high on the bat and rolls over to vacant short square leg region.
Neil Wagner walks out to bat!

OUT! TAKEN! Mitchell is a goner and Stone gets a wicket quickly after the break. Just the start his side would have wanted. This is short and on middle, Mitchell looks to pull but it goes more off the upper part and straight to mid-wicket. England into the bowling all-rounders now. Lead is just the 32.
Commentary.Howout: c Zak Crawley b Olly Stone

Commentary.Commentary: On middle. It is worked towards square leg for a single.
FOUR LEG BYES! Back of a length ball, drifting it on the leg side. Blundell looks to clip but misses, hits his pads, and the ball rolls over to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Length ball, on middle. It is clipped towards mid-wicket.
Tad fuller and nips in on middle. Blundell solidly defends it.
A length ball, on off. Mitchell looks to defend but it goes off the outer half towards the gully region for a couple of runs.
Full and around off. Mitchell shimmies down to block it towards cover.
On middle. Blocked out.
Length ball and angles it on middle. It is defended towards mid-on.
A length ball, and on middle. Mitchell defends it on the pitch.
Length ball, and on off. Blocked out.
James Anderson to bowl from the other end!
A dot to end! On middle, blocked.
Mitchell too scored his first run of the session. Stone goes wide of the crease and angles it into the pads, it is worked through square leg for one.
First run in this session! On middle, this is worked towards mid-wicket for one.
Back of a length and on middle, blocked.
On the fuller side but a little too straight, it is worked to mid-wicket.
Starts off on a length and outside off, left alone.

We are all set for the action to begin! The England players make their way out to the middle. They are followed by the New Zealand batters, Mitchell and Blundell who will continue their innings. Olle Stone to bowl.
... Day 3, Session 2 ...

The Black Caps would be looking to just bat on and on. One more session with the bat should take the lead beyond 100 which would prove very substantial on this pitch. But they have their last recognized batting pair in the middle. They would hope that it digs in and forms a big partnership. Join us back at 1.40 pm local (1240 GMT) for the second session.

End of a very good session for New Zealand. They have scored 97 runs and lost 2 wickets and got into the lead. The pitch still looks good to bat on what could be the best batting day of the match. England could have had more wickets, but for their poor catching. However, they are not far behind the 8-ball and will look forward to break this Blundell-Mitchell stand as quickly as possible and keep the lead under say, 75.
On a good length, outside off, moving away, Mitchell works it with the away movement towards third man for a couple. LUNCH ON DAY 3, NEW ZEALAND LEAD BY 23!
Around off, on a length, solidly defended.
A short ball, outside off, pulled towards long leg for a single.
Full and wide outside off, left alone.
On a good length, outside off, Tom Blundell defends solidly.
Around off, angling in, worked through mid-wicket for a couple. The lead moves to 20. The stand moves to 11.
Should be the last over before Lunch. Just a minute left.
Short, outside off, punched towards short extra cover.
Tossed up, outside off, Daryl Mitchell comes down the track but yorks himself. Gets an inside edge onto his pads.
Short, outside off, worked through mid-wicket for a single.
Around middle, looped up a touch, worked in front of short leg. 3 minutes to go for Lunch.
Outside off, solidly blocked.
Full, around off, pushed to the right of Joe Root.
5 minutes to go to Lunch. Joe Root brings himself on. 13-3-39-0 so far.
Oohhh.. this seemed like a plan. Wood bowls a ball down the leg side, a full toss and Mitchell misses his flick. Interestingly, Joe Root has stationed himself at leg slip.
Full, outside off, Daryl Mitchell walks forward and defends.
A bouncer, but down the leg side, ducked under.
7 minutes to go to Lunch. James Anderson is warming up.
Full, outside off, watchfully kept out.
Around off, on a length, solidly defended.
Around off, angling in, worked through mid-wicket for a single. Moves to 20.
Another bouncer, this time Daryl ducks.
A bouncer outside off, Mitchell pulls out of the pull.
Around off, tucked towards short mid-wicket for a run.

Oh dear. We have a delay. As the ball touched the fence, someone at the periphery touched it and returned the ball. Now, due to the new Covid rules, the on-field people cannot touch the ball now and have to disinfect it. The umpires are in the middle, they look at the ball but cannot touch it, till eventually, they get a cloth to wipe it and then hand it over to Stone.
FOUR! BRUTAL! That is a bad ball. Short, wide outside off and punished. Tom Blundell crashes a cut through point.
Outside off, a short length ball, Daryl Mitchell nudges it through square leg and now gets off the mark.
Around off, pushed towards mid on.
A short ball, outside off, skids through, Blundell looks to pull but misses and is hit on the pads. End of a good, hostile over from Wood.
Around off, pushed towards short mid-wicket.
A short ball, outside off, pulled wide of short mid-wicket.
He is away straigthaway. Around off, Daryl Mitchell gets across and nudges it towards fine leg. Oh wait. It is a leg bye. Mitchell stays on 0 then.
Daryl Mitchell walks in at number 7, replacing Henry Nicholls. Didn't play at Lord's but the last time he did play a Test, scored a century. It was at Wellington, in January 2021, against Pakistan.

OUT! GLOVED DOWN THE LEG SIDE! Wood strikes now and two set batsmen are back in the pavillon. A short ball, down the leg side, angled in from around the wicket, Henry Nicholls gets across to nudge it fine. But instead, all he manages is a tickle off the gloves and keeper James Bracey does the rest, going down to his right. England appeal, umpire Richard Kettleborough has his finger raised but Nicholls does not wait. He was off as soon as he saw the catch getting completed. End of a watchful knock.
Commentary.Howout: c James Bracey b Mark Wood

Commentary.Commentary: The physio is coming out. Nicholls says he is okay but he has to pass the mandatory concussion test. Which he does and we are ready.

OUCH! Onto the helmet. A short ball, around off, Henry Nicholls looks to pull but the ball comes on much quicker than his anticipation and hits him on the helmet. Perhaps he took his eyes off the ball too.

FOUR! Good punch down the ground. Full, outside off, Tom Blundell comes forward and just pushes this down the ground, without any big followthrough and wide mid off has no chance. The stand moves to 20.
Around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Full, outside off, driven straight to mid off.
On a length, outside off, solidly defended.
Down the leg side, Nicholls look to flick but misses. The ball goes off his pads towards square leg. No signal from the umpire, so must have been an inside edge.
Outside off, on a length, Henry Nicholls shoulders arms.
Around off, tucked towards short mid-wicket.

FOUR! Starting to feel a little more comfortable, is Tom Blundell. Outside off, on a length, Blundell opens the face of his bat and guides it behind point. He moves to 10 and NEW ZEALAND ARE INTO THE LEAD.

Ha ha ha. Spends a lot of time on the floor after he delivers, Mark Wood. Full, outside off, Tom Blundell drives it straight back. Wood slips in his followthrough but keeps his eyes on the ball and collects it as it comes right at his face.
Full, outside off, angling in, pushed towards mid on.
Around middle, angled in, tucked towards deep mid-wicket for a single. NEW ZEALAND DRAW PARITY. Nicholls moves to 20.
Outside off, on a length, left alone.
Full, outside off, solidly blocked.
A short ball, around off, Henry pulls it towards deep mid-wicket for a run. The stand moves to 10.
Down the leg side, angled in from around the wicket, Nicholls misses his tuck.
Around middle, Tom Blundell looks to tuck but misses. The ball hits his pads and drops down to the leg side. Blundell looks up at Nicholls, who calls him through. A leg bye taken.
Full, around off, solidly defended.
300 COMES UP FOR NEW ZEALAND. They trail by 3 now. Around middle, nudged through square leg for a single.

FOUR! Nicely played. On a length, outside off, Tom Blundell allows the ball to come to him, sees it move away and then at the last moment, dabs it wide of gully, to his left, to find the fence at third man.
Fuller, outside off, left alone.
A bouncer, around middle, Blundell ducks.
This one comes back in from a length, outside off, Tom Blundell defends it watchfully.
Back of a length, outside off, pushed towards cover.
On a good length, outside off, pushed towards point.
Landed outside off, on a length, left alone. Pretty wide to be playing those.
Full, outside off, shouldered arms to.
Around off, nudged through square leg for a single.

On a good length, around off, Blundell tucks it towards square leg. Henry Nicholls scampers through for the single, before being sent back at the last moment. The throw misses the stumps at the bowler's end.
Outside off, on a length, left alone.

On a good length, outside off, Tom Blundell shoulders arms. The ball jags back in tremendously and Blundell is hit on the thigh pads. Olly Stone thinks he has his man and screams for the LBW. Denied by the umpire. Stone looks at his skipper who indicates height.
A bouncer, down the leg side, let through.
Outside off, pushed wide of mid off, to his left, for a quick single. Good stop by James Anderson. The deficit is now 9. Blundell is off the mark.
Around off, pushed towards mid on.
Outside off, on a length, Tom Blundell feels for it but misses.
Around middle, nudged towards fine leg for a single.
Around middle, pushed towards mid on.

EDGED, DROPPED! The second chance goes off Stone in this Test. Young, on Friday and Bracey now. England have been poor with their catching - full stop. Full, outside off, Tom Blundell looks to defend but the ball moves away and takes an outside edge. It is a wide ball to be defending at and Blundell nearly pays the price. But James Bracey dives to his right with one glove and cannot hang on. End of a successful over nevertheless from Stone. Could have had two.
Outside off again, on a length, left alone again.
Outside off, moving away, left alone.
Tom Blundell walks in at number 6, replacing Ross Taylor.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Another batsman falls in the 80s in this Test. Rory Burns, Dan Lawrence (stranded), Devon Conway, Will Young and now, Ross Taylor. Not a special ball by any means but Olly Stone will take it. Full, outside off, moving away slightly, Taylor, looking to keep up with his aggressive intent, slashes hard, without any footwork. Gets a thick outside edge and James Bracey, the keeper, does well to get across to his right to take it. Edgbaston erupts. Ollie leaps. England get a breakthrough right after Drinks. They lead by 11 and have an inexperienced lower middle order in front of them.
Commentary.Howout: c James Bracey b Olly Stone

Commentary.Commentary: Seems like a part of the leather has come off the ball. The umpire cuts it off with a scissor.
Full, around off, pushed towards mid on.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Olly Stone comes into the attack now. 15-4-58-0 so far.

DRINKS BREAK. New Zeaand's hour, without a doubt. Things could have been different though, had England held onto their chance. Ross Taylor has come out with an attacking mode and he is actually taking this game away from England. The deficit is almost negligible and another hour of such batting might swell the lead to 50. England have some thinking to do and they bowlers other than Stuart Broad to step up.
Full, around off, nudged towards fine leg for a run.
Outside off, on a length, Ross Taylor sets himself up for the pull but then adjusts and defends it down the track.
This one swings in, from outside off, Nicholls works it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.

FOUR! No third man and that is an advantage sometimes in Test matches. Outside off, Henry Nicholls leans, opens the face of the bat and guides it to the left of backward point, to the third man fence. The stand moves to 61.
Outside off, extra bounce, pushed towards point.
Umpire Richard Kettleborough is looking concerned. He walks down the middle of the pitch, looks at the area and gives a friendly warning to Wood. Oh my. Wood has run straight down the pitch.
Around middle, tucked towards square leg.
Change in the bowling. Mark Wood to bowl. 14-0-43-0 so far.

FOUR! Gets this one through. Taylor is really looking good this morning. Full, outside off, Ross Taylor leans and drives this through mid off. Stuart Broad lumbers to his left and puts in a laboured dive and misses. The deficit is now 17.
Angled into the left hander, tucked towards fine leg for a single.
On a good length, around off, solidly defended.

That is a good shot. Full, outside off, Taylor leans into the shot and pushes it through mid off. Stuart Broad goes after it but Mark Wood gets there first, from mid on. Slides and parries it back to Broad. Three runs taken. 50-STAND IS UP! Nicholls' contribution is just 10.
Well fielded. Short, outside off, Ross Taylor nails the cut this time. And it is Zak Crawley once again! At point, who dives to his right and stops it with one hand.
Full, around off, worked towards mid on.

Three times in a row as far as this shot is concerned. Short, outside off, Ross pulls it through mid-wicket but Zak Crawley dives to his left and makes a half stop, parrying it to the right of mid on. A single taken.
Landed outside off, Rosco walks into the shot and pushes it through mid off. James Anderson gets across to his right from wide mid off and stops it.
That's twice in two overs. Short, outside off, Ross Taylor pulls it away but finds Zak Crawley at short mid-wicket.
A short ball, around middle and leg, nudged towards fine leg for a run. Nicholls moves to 10.
Outside off, pushed towards cover for a single.

FOUR BYES! James Bracey is having a nightmare behind the stumps. A length ball, outside off, Ross Taylor shoulders arms. The ball goes through but keeps on climbing towards Bracey who is certainly not expecting it. The ball hits the top of his gloves and flies down to the third man fence. The deficit is now 28.
Full, outside off, watchfully defended.
Around middle, well defended.

Outside off, on a length, coming in, once again Henry Nicholls trusts the bounce and shoulders arms. The ball justifies his trust and goes over the off stump. Keeper James Bracey has to dive to his right to stop and fumbles.
Outside off, pushed towards point for a single. Taylor moves to 70.
And again. Full and down the leg side, Ross Taylor misses his flick again.
Down the leg side, flick shot missed.

Huge shout for LBW but turned down. Pitched outside leg to the naked eye. Nicholls missed his tuck and was hit on the pads. Broad wants a review but Joe Root convinces him that it pitched outside leg. Ball Tracker confirms.
FOUR BYES! More frustration for Stuart Broad. A short ball, around middle, Henry Nicholls ducks and the ball shoots well above him and the keeper to the fence behind. The stand moves to 41.

DROPPED! Rosco gets a life. A short ball, around off, Taylor looks to pull but the bounce does him in. The ball goes towards fine leg where substitute Sam Billings runs in to take the catch. Gets to the ball but it goes right between his hands and drops down. A single taken.
Missed out. A short ball, outside off, Ross Taylor nails the pull to perfection but finds Zak Crawley to perfection at short mid-wicket. A meter either side of him and it was a boundary.
Around middle, tucked through square leg for a quick run.

Around off, coming in, worked through mid-wicket. Bit of a misfield from Zak Crawley coming in, which makes it easier for the single to be completed. Took his eyes off the ball and missed it. The deficit is now 39.
Full, around off, solidly defended.
Outside off, on a length, Nicholls shoulders arms.
Around middle, pushed to the leg side.

Outside off, angled in, Henry Nicholls misses his tuck and is hit on the pads. The ball hits the thigh and balloons towards gully. The crowd gets excited when the catch is taken and James Anderson makes a polite enquiry for the catch. Umpire Richard Illingworth is not interested.
Outside off, pushed towards cover.
The umpire has a look at the ball, to check whether it has gone out of shape. Nope, nothing. Please continue.

Full, outside off, Ross Taylor drives this straight back. Good athleticism from James Anderson to get his foot in the way. The ball actually hits the sole of the boot and deflects wide of Stuart Broad at mid off, who was going to his right, but then has to move to his left. A single taken.
Fuller, around off, pushed towards point.
Good pace, short and directed at Henry's arm pit, the southpaw thinks about pulling but then lets it go.
Comes from over the wicket, angles this away from the left hander, Nicholls lets it go.
Fuller, around off, whipped through mid-wicket where Dan Lawrence dives to his left and makes a good stop.
This one has extra bounce, around off, Henry Nicholls hops and defends.
Landed outside off, on a length, left alone.
Fuller, around off, watchfully kept out.
Around off, solidly defended.

FOUR MORE! Much better from Taylor. On a length, outside off, this time Ross Taylor waits for the ball to come to him and punches this off the back foot, well in front of point, for consecutive boundaries. The stand moves to 33 from just 37 balls.

EDGED, FOUR! Flashy from Rosco. Full, wide outside off, Ross Taylor looks to drive this on the up. The ball moves away, takes the outside edge and flies through backward point. Rory Burns dives to his right but the ball is past him in a flash. Taylor moves to 62.
Around off, moving away, watchfully pushed towards point.
On a length, around off, watchfully defended.
Little bit quicker, but wider outside off, shouldered arms to.
Around off, on a length, left alone.

Full, outside off, Taylor drives this with the full face of the bat, straight back to the bowler. Stuart Broad saves his face by getting his hands in front, through pure reflex action. The ball bursts through his fingers and goes down the ground. Mark Wood does well to get across from mid on and slide to keep the batsmen to a single. The deficit is now 49.
Full, just outside off, Ross Taylor plays this with a straight bat towards mid on.

Short, a little bit wide outside off, Henry Nicholls stands tall, gets on top of the bounce and punches it through the covers. Ollie Pope gets to the ball and slides, parrying the ball to the fielder running with him from point. Three runs taken.
Down the leg side, left alone.
Outside off, angling away, left alone.
Sprayed down the leg side, HN misses his flick and James Bracey cannot stop it cleanly even with a dive to his right. A bye conceded. 250 UP FOR NEW ZEALAND. Trail by 53.
Good carry again. On a length, outside off, coming in with the angle, Henry trusts the bounce and shoulders arms. The ball clips his left trouser and goes over the stumps to the keeper.
A short ball, around middle, Nicholls leaps and fends it down to the leg side. The pitch seems to have gotten quicker.
This is wider outside off, Henry Nicholls thinks of going after it with a cut but pulls his bat back at the last moment.
On a length, around off, watchfully defended.
The second new ball is available and IT IS TAKEN. James Anderson will bowl first with the new cherry. 18-5-45-0 so far.
Onto the helmet. A short ball, around off, coming in, Ross leaps to fend it away but gets a top edge and the ball deflects onto the grill.
Around off, length pulled back slightly, Rosco walks across and pushes this towards mid on.
FOUR! MARVELLOUS! Overpitched, outside off, Taylor leans and drives it to the left of mid off. The stand moves to 20 from 19 balls.
Around off, pushed to the off side.
Straighter, around off, watchfully pushed towards short mid-wicket.
Full, around middle, Ross Taylor looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. Going down leg.
Looped up, around leg, defended towards shrt mid-wicket.
Outside off, pushed towards point for one.
Short, outside off, Henry Nicholls rocks back and cuts it through the covers for a run.
Outside off, cut through point for a single.

FOUR! No arguments this time! FIFTY FOR ROSCO! Full, outside off, Taylor gets down and sweeps this powerfully through square leg. It has been a scratchy innings but runs are runs. He will take them all the more. Can he get to his century now?

FOUR! Fifty for Ross Taylor. Or is it? Nope. LEG BYES signalled. Full, around middle, spinning down, Ross Taylor looks to flick and the ball goes off something, through the vacant leg slip region to the fine leg fence. Now, Taylor is ready to raise his bat but then he sees the umpire signal it as leg byes. Ultra Edge later on shows there was an inside edge!
Will Lawrence get another over? Yes.
Full again, outside off, Nicholls drives this solidly towards mid off.
Fuller, around middle, driven towards mid on.
Around off, pushed towards mid off.
Around off, angling in, watchfully defended.

NOT OUT. Joe Root shakes his head. Not because this was not out but because of the ease with which the batsmen got a single. Outside off, Ross Taylor pushes it towards cover and sets off for a quick single. The fielder gets to his right from point and has a shy at the striker's end and hits. Referred upstairs but Nicholls was well in. The deficit is now 69.
Direct hit but Nicholls looks in. As per the rule, this needs to go upstairs and it does. Replay is conclusive.
Full, around middle, clipped through mid-wicket. Plenty of vacant real estate there and the batsmen take three.
It will be Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end. 15-6-22-2 so far.
Full, around off, watchfully defended.
A full bunger, around middle, Henry Nicholls gets down and sweeps it through square leg for a single. Off the mark.
Full, around off, watchfully defended.
All set then, for the game to resume? The players are out in the middle. The new man in is Henry Nicholls while Dan Lawrence will finish off his pending over. Here we go...

If any, New Zealand would be ruing the last-ball wicket of Will Young on Friday evening, just about marring what was an excellent day's work. They have got plenty of batting left, in Henry Nicholls, Tom Blundell and Daryl Mitchell, but some inexperience as well. They have Ross Taylor batting well on 46, but everyday is a new day and England will know that if they get Taylor early, or go through his partners, they might well even get a lead, however slender it might be. The bowlers endured a tough day on Friday and would want to make amends on Saturday. Anticipating an exciting session.

A day of the 'Young'sters it was. First Devon Conway. Then, Will Young. The young pair first took New Zealand to the shores of safety and then started to impress themselves against a rampant Stuart Broad. New Zealand trail by just 74 now, but we all know how batting collapses are just on the verge of happening. Who will make the first move on the moving day? Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of the second Test between England and New Zealand, at Edgbaston, Birmingham.

Now what would the teams want on Day 3? The Kiwis would want to just bat, bat and bat and try and take a lead of over 100. England can't afford that as the pitch has started to show some wear and tear and any sort of lead would be handy. Another important day awaits. Do join us. Till then, take care and goodbye!

The England bowlers did not bowl that badly, they caused a lot of problems, beat the edge a lot of times but they just did not have a lot of luck on their side. Broad though was the pick for them. He looked threatening in every spell he bowled and has two out of the three wickets to fall.

Another session which goes their way! They lost Conway early on but after that, Ross and Young battled through the difficult part and then managed to score freely. They added another good stand and got the deficit to below 80. Just as it seemed that both would resume their innings on Day 3, Young fell.

End of a really good day of Test cricket and on the end, it is New Zealand who will be the happier of the two. They would have been a lot more pleased had that wicket not fallen but the visitors will be pretty happy with where they are in the game at the moment.

OUT! TAKEN AT BAT-PAD! Lawrence strikes on the last over of the day and Young is the one to depart. First Test wicket for Lawrence and the move to give him the ball proves to be a master stroke. Big turn on this one. It lands outside off, in the rough and turns back in. Young lunges to defend but it goes off the inside edge and lobs towards short leg where the fielder dives forward and takes it. Heartbreak for Young as he trudges off slowly. THAT WILL ALSO BE STUMPS ON DAY 2!
Commentary.Howout: c Ollie Pope b Dan Lawrence

... Day 2, Session 3 ...

England on the other hand, bowled well initially but the quality kept fading as the session went on. There were far too many loose balls and boundaries were also being scored frequently. They need to get a couple of wickets quickly or they will be chasing the game. Will there be a fight back? We will find out.

The session though started with England getting a chance to dismiss Young but that was not taken and since then, it was all about the two. They weathered the storm earlier on and then played brilliantly. As the innings progressed, they managed to score freely too. Conway has got to a half ton and Young is nearing his. The stand is above 100 and New Zealand will love another session like this one.
That is a superb session for the Kiwis! The two newbies to Test cricket, Young and Conway, have shown excellent technique and have really taken the visitors into a good position.

Not started well in this over. Another one down the leg side, this time it goes to the keeper as Young misses the flick.
Two more to the score then in the form of leg byes! On the pads, this goes off the pads as Young looks to flick. Towards fine leg for two.

FOUR! A boundary to end and the pressure that was building has been released a little. 6 from the over. This is bread and butter stuff for Conway. Full and on off, he leans into it and strokes it through covers for a boundary.
Slightly shorter this time, Devon hangs back and blocks it.
Well bowled! Switches to around the wicket and angles this into middle, Conway looks to defend but this goes off the inner half towards square leg.
Shorter and on off, this moves away late. Conway adjusts and blocks it onto the ground.
Finally some runs for New Zealand! Just a mere push there! On off, this is pushed past mid off for two.
This is in the 5th stump channel outside off, Conway covers his off pole and lets it be.
Another dot and England continue to build the pressure with another maiden! On off, blocked.
Now goes for the tempter, it is full and outside off, shaping away too. Stone is not tempted and he left it alone.
Better length but the line is a little too straight this time, it is worked to mid on.
A little bit shorter this time and a touch easier for Young to play it. He defends it on the leg side with ease.
Relentless stuff from Stone too. He too gives nothing away. Attacks the off pole, blocked.
Really good! Hits the length, attacks the off pole. Gets it to jag back in a little. Young tries to defend but gets an inside edge onto the pads.
Back-to-back maidens then for England. On off, Conway plays it to covers.
Relentless stuff from James. He bowls the middle stump line again and on a length. Conway keeps it out.
Really solid! Shorter again and on off, Conway drops it on the off side, he wants a run but is sent back rightly.
And again, plays it late, right under his eyes, this is shorter. Kept out.
This time Conway lets the ball come to him, watches it and then plays it late and onto the ground.

Beauty again! The ball is moving around now, just like it was yesterday when the Kiwis were bowling in the second session. On off and it shapes away. Conway looks to block but this one whizzes past the outside edge.
A solid defensive stroke to end a testing over by Stone. He should have had a wicket but that's not the case.
An absolute beauty! Unplayable. You just have to hope it does not take the edge. On off and on a length, pitches and moves away. Young is beaten all ends up as he tries to block.
On middle, this one is defended right off the middle to mid on.

THAT'S IN, NO, IT HAS BEEN PUT DOWN! Root at first slip is the culprit. That is a regulation slip catch. On a length and around off, this one holds its line. Young looks to defend but it goes off the outside edge to Root at first slips. He has a couple of attempts at it but spills it. A life for Young. Can he make use of it.
A sharp short one, Young picks it early and ducks under it.
Goes wide of the crease and angles it into middle, kept out.
FOUR! Catch it is the call but there's no one close to it. Short and on the body, this is pulled fine and it races away to the fence on the leg side. 50 up with that boundary.
Another back of a length ball, Conway takes one hand off the handle and keeps it out.
Pushes this one across the left-hander. Conway stands tall and blocks it.
Drop and run! On off, Young plays it towards point for one.
On the off pole this time, Young hangs back and keeps it out.
Starts off with a gentle medium pace ball outside off, Young covers his off pole and leaves it alone.
James Anderson to bowl from the other end.
Attacks the stumps to end the over! This is worked to mid-wicket.
Better! Back of a length and on off, Conway plays it late and onto the ground off the back foot.
One more harmless nut outside off, left alone.

FOUR! Sheer timing! Just used the pace of the bowler and it is a fabulous way to score the first runs after the break! Length and on off, Conway just puts bat on ball, he creams it through covers for a boundary.
Some excitement from the fielders but nothing from the keeper and the bowler. This is down the leg side, Conway misses the flick. The ball swings away. The keeper dives and takes it.
Starts off with a harmless delivery but at a good pace, 86 MPH. Outside off, left alone.
We are back for the afternoon session, another important one. The two batsmen, Conway and Young will resume their innings. Stone to begin proceedings for England. Here we go...
... Day 2, Session 2 ...

It actually has all been about Stuart Broad. No other bowler has got as much movement as Broad has and the Kiwis might just be smart enough to see him off and score against the other bowlers. There isn't any swing and if the sun comes out, batting gets easier. Join us at 1.40 pm local (1240 GMT) for all the action from the second session.

New Zealand would be happy to have lost just Latham before Lunch. Playing Broad in this kind of form is menacing and Devon Conway has done really well to see off this period. He received a big slice of luck with a controversial catch but these things happen. Will Young has looked solid in his short stay so far.

End of an intriguing session. England came out all guns blazing, trying to get quick runs and got past 300. Then, with the ball, Stuart Broad generated excellent rhythm by striking in his third over. He would argue that he should have had two wickets but technology will not agree. Anderson was okay at the other end but not his usual self.
Tempter, half volley outside off, Young lets it pass. LUNCH ON DAY 2, NEW ZEALAND 43/1, TRAIL BY 260.
Full, around off, pushed towards point. Young wants the single but Conway is not running.
A short ball now, Conway swivels and pulls it, to the left of the man at backward square leg, for a single to long leg.
Full and gun-barrel straight, watchfully defended towards mid on.
Around off, blocked to the off side.
Full, around middle, Devon Conway plays a flamingo flick, with his left leg coming up in the air. The ball goes behind square leg and the batsmen take a couple.
Possibly the last over before Lunch...
Full, wide outside off, driven straight to cover.
Around off, driven straight to mid off.
FOUR! Missed out off Broad in the previous over but does not miss out this time. Stone gets a bit too straight and Will Young clips it off his pads through square leg.

On a length, around middle, Devon Conway comes forward, looks to defend but is squared up as the ball moves away late. Gets an outside edge through point and the batsmen take a single. This is a good start from Stone.
Around off, angling away, pushed to the off side.
Full, around off, pushed towards cover.
Here comes Olly Stone on his home ground. 6 minutes to go for Lunch.
Around off, solidly defended.
Around off, coming in, Will Young looks to defend but misses and gets hit on the pads. Broad starts to go up in an appeal but then realizes the inside edge.
Full, around off, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.

Very good running. Smart cricket. Outside off, Conway just pushes it to the right of mid off and scampers across for a single. Conway will hope Young sees off the remainder of the Broad over. The stand moves to 20.
Angled down the leg side, Devon Conway misses his tuck and is hit on the pads.
Good length, outside off, left alone.
Good length ball, around off, solidly defended.
On a good length, outside off, Young shoulders arms. The ball does come in, but goes well past the off stump.
Around off, watchfully blocked out.
Off the mark, is Young. Gets across and nurdles this through square leg, for a couple. The deficit is now 269.
Around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Around middle, Will Young misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Fuller, around middle, pushed towards mid on.
Around off, pushed towards mid off.
Down the leg side, nudged towards square leg.
Around off, pushed towards mid off.

NOT OUT. Stuart Broad is not happy. The Edgbaston crowd is not happy. A length ball, outside off, Devon Conway lunged to push at it. But the ball spit off the deck and Conway got hit high on the bat. The ball flew off the outside edge towards Zak Crawley at third slip. Now, Crawley claimed it, to have taken inches above the ground but Conway was going nowhere. At full speed, the umpires felt that the ball had bounced and even during the replays, the third umpire did not have concrete evidence to overturn the decision. Some might argue that Crawley had his fingers underneath the ball, but very difficult to say. From the front-on angle, the ball seemed to have bounced.

Is that taken? Did it carry? The umpires have a chat. The soft signal is NOT OUT. The third umpire has to have convincing evidence to overturn this decision and give Conway out. Seems to have bounced (to my naked eye). The third umpire agrees. I can potspone my visit to the doctor then...
Around off, left alone.
Down the leg side, Will Young misses his flick and the ball goes off his pads through square leg. Two leg byes taken to end a scrappy opening over from Wood. 13 from the over.
Durham vs Durham now. Wood and Young play for the same side in County cricket and would know each other pretty well.

Ooohh... inside edge... past the stumps! Around off, Devon pushes forward but not with total conviction. There is a gap between bat and pad and the ball takes that, off the inside edge and scoots past the off stump towards fine leg. A single taken.
Aroud off, solidly defended.
Wood is changing the angle now, coming around the wicket.

FOUR! Mark Wood needs to be careful here, with the ball not swinging. His length cannot be too full. Outside off, Devon Conway leans and drives it through point this time, for consecutive boundaries. Moves to 21.

Wood loses his runup. That's twice now, in 2 balls. The wind is going across his body and it is pretty strong. Meanwhile, the swing has disappeared along with the disappearing overcast conditions and Joe Root takes gully off.
FOUR! MAJESTIC! Overpitched, wide outside off, Conway leans and drives it through the covers, getting it past the diving fielder.
Full, outside off, Devon Conway leans and drives this through the covers. Gets a couple.

England seem to be hustling through their overs. The 40 percent fine after the first match seems to have had an impact on the players. Here comes the first bowling change, who anyway hustles through his bowling. Mark Wood into the attack.
Full, around off, better defensive shot from Will, getting nicely forward and being compact.
Good length ball, outside off, pushed towards cover.
Around off, on a length, solidly defended.
That is a jaffa. On a length, outside off, Young looks to defend but is beaten by pace comprehensively.
Around off, solidly defended.
Full, around off, Will Young walks into the shot and pushes it towards cover.
Back of a length, around middle, jabbed to the off side.
Another good looking block to the off side by DC.
Pushed to the cover region, this time.
On a length, around off, skids through, across the left hander, Conway pushes but misses.
FOUR! MAGNIFICENT! We saw plenty of this at Lord's. Full, outside off, Devon Conway comes forward and drives this crisply through the covers. Moves to 11.
Full, outside off, pushed defensively towards point.
Full and outside off, Will Young looks to defend but is late and gets beaten. A run and a wicket from the over.
Outside off, on a length, left alone.
Big boots to fill. Will Young walks in at number 3, replacing Kane Williamson for this Test match. Pressure on the newbie.

OUT! LBW! That is dead plumb. Broad strikes early. Full, straight, outside off, coming in, Tom Latham tries to defend by coming forward but misses the line of the ball, getting pinged on the pads. Broad knows he has his man and appeals. Umpire Richard Kettleborough raises his finger in a flash. Latham walks down to have a chat with Conway and then after a brief discussion, starts walking off. Good decision not to review. Ball Tracker shows that to be taking out leg stump.
Fuller, wider, in that fourth stump channel, TL raises his blade and lets the ball pass.
Bowls it from slightly outside the crease, but fires this straight on the pads. Again, Devon gets hit on the pad and he sneaks a leg bye as the ball goes behind square on the leg side.
Full, around off, flicked straight to mid-wicket.
Down the leg side, Conway looks to tuck it away but misses. The ball hits his thigs and deflects towards the keeper. Slightly wide. A leg bye taken. The deficit is now 289.
Around middle, pushed to the off side.
Around middle and leg, nudged to the leg side.
Fuller, outside off, Devon Conway feels for it but misses.
On a good length now, outside off, let through once again.
Around off, angling away, left alone.
Full, outside off, left alone.
Outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Around off, flicked straight to square leg.
Around off, pushed to the off side.
Outside off, left alone.

That would have been a very, very unlucky way to go. Full, around off, Tom Latham drove it straight back. Stuart Broad got across to his left, got fingertips onto the ball and it hit the stumps. Broad and England got very excited and so did the crowd, once it saw the ball brushing Broad's fingers, on the giant screen. The third umpire wanted to check what happened next. What came next? The ball, or the bat? The bat. Got dragged into the crease and then the ball hit the stumps at the bowler's end.
Is that a run out? Broad seems excited (of course, he always is) and umpire Kettleborough takes it upstairs. Here comes the replay - SAFE!
Outside off, left alone.
Around middle, helped through square leg for a single.
On a good length, around middle, Tom lets it pass once more.
Angling away, full outside off again, this time, Latham shoulders arms.
FOUR! LOVELY! Full, outside off, Tom Latham comes forward and drives it straight back past the bowler, down the ground, through the vacant mid off region. Supreme shot. The stand moves to 12.
Full, outside off, angling away, let through.
Outside off, left alone.
Aound off, defended solidly.
Full, outside off, left alone.
Around off, Devon Conway looks to defend but gets an inside edge to the leg side.
A length ball now, tucked behind square leg for a couple.
FOUR! Fine shot. Full, angling in, flicked through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.
Around off, pushed to the off side for a quick single. Both openers are away.
Outside off, left alone.
Full outside off, pushed towards cover.
Around middle, flicked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Outside off, swinging but wider, left alone.
Full, outside off, left alone.
